target: Weather first, at the learner’s level: Curious, Drone, Student, Commercial, Airline and Defence. The live map is the lab.

modes.live-chart: The stem and the key are computed from the current Isobar store (ECMWF run, METAR, TAF, SIGMET). A card that cannot be recomputed is not served.
modes.physics-why: The scored claim is a mechanism. Today's chart may be the stem. The key does not depend on a number that will be different tomorrow.
modes.bank-only: Law, a copyrighted exam chart, or a procedure that needs an aircraft or a route the store does not have. Original questions only. Never a recalled exam item.

layers.isobars: MSLP lines on the playing map
layers.wind: Wind-speed colour field and wind barbs
layers.fly: Fly lens: METAR, TAF groups, runway components, SIGMET
layers.upper-point: IFS upper-air point at YPPH or YSSY. Not a map layer yet.
layers.none: No map product can show this

concepts.title: Highs, lows and the MSLP field
concepts.au_us: Same chart reading. Australian analyses are in hPa. A US altimeter subscale is in inches of mercury; 1013.25 hPa is 29.92 inHg.

concepts.title: Isobar spacing is the pressure gradient
concepts.au_us: Shared. Tight spacing means a strong gradient in both syllabi.

concepts.title: Coriolis and why the hemisphere matters
concepts.au_us: The deflection is to the left in Australia and to the right in the contiguous United States. A northern-hemisphere diagram with the labels swapped is a wrong answer, not a translation.

concepts.title: Geostrophic balance
concepts.au_us: Shared balance. In the southern hemisphere the high is on the left of the geostrophic wind. US teaching diagrams usually show the high on the right.

concepts.title: Gradient wind around curved isobars
concepts.au_us: Shared. Around a low, gradient wind is slower than geostrophic; around a high it is faster. The store can score a geostrophic estimate from MSLP. It cannot yet score curvature, so a live card must say geostrophic and keep the curved-flow correction for the reveal.

concepts.title: Why the surface wind is not the gradient wind
concepts.au_us: Shared. Friction slows the wind and turns it toward lower pressure. The cross-isobar angle is a teaching range, not a constant to memorise as law.

concepts.title: Wind at your back, low on the right (southern hemisphere)
concepts.au_us: The Australian rule is low on the right. The US rule is low on the left. These are not the same sentence with a place name changed.

concepts.title: Temperature, the ISA and the lapse rate
concepts.au_us: Shared ISA (15 °C and 1013.25 hPa at sea level, lapse about 2 °C per 1,000 ft). Australian METARs report °C and hPa. US METARs report °C and inches of mercury.

concepts.title: Dewpoint, spread and where cloud can form
concepts.au_us: Shared. A small temperature-dewpoint spread means the air is close to saturation. It does not by itself mean a ceiling.

concepts.title: ELR against the dry and saturated adiabatic lapse rates
concepts.au_us: Shared. Dry adiabatic lapse rate about 3 °C per 1,000 ft; saturated about 1.5 °C per 1,000 ft in the teaching model. Absolutely unstable means the environment cools faster than the dry rate.

concepts.title: Lift, instability and moisture
concepts.au_us: Shared ingredients. MUCAPE is in the ECMWF grid and is not yet a map colour. The SIGMET is the evidence that lift is already occurring. A high-CAPE cell with no SIGMET is not a storm on the chart.

concepts.title: Ceiling is BKN or OVC, not FEW or SCT
concepts.au_us: Shared cloud-amount rule. Australian TAFs add INTER and use CAVOK. US TAFs do not.

concepts.title: FM, BECMG, TEMPO, INTER and PROB
concepts.au_us: INTER is Australian (and ICAO) and is not a US TAF group. CAVOK is used in Australian METAR and TAF and is not used in US METAR. TEMPO and FM exist in both. A card graded on an Australian TAF must not treat INTER as TEMPO, and a US card must not offer CAVOK as a choice.

concepts.title: Freezing level and airframe ice
concepts.au_us: Shared physics. The store's freezing level is metres from the Open-Meteo point. Australian area forecasts often give it in feet. Convert; do not mix the units in the key.

concepts.title: SIGMET turbulence and where the shear is
concepts.au_us: Both states issue ICAO SIGMETs. The Australian products in this store are for YMMM and YBBB. A US convective SIGMET is a different product with a different shape. Do not grade one against the other's template.

concepts.title: Fronts and troughs as a change of air mass
concepts.au_us: Shared model of a front. The store has no analysed front polylines. A live card must not invent a front position from isobar kinks.

concepts.title: UTC on the product, local time at the aerodrome
concepts.au_us: Products are in UTC. Perth is Australia/Perth, no daylight saving. Sydney is Australia/Sydney and observes daylight saving. A US cross-country uses the same UTC rule and a different set of zones.

concepts.title: Great circle and rhumb line
concepts.au_us: Shared geometry. The ATPL navigation exam also examines the chart projections and the calculations. Those stay bank-only until a route exists.

concepts.title: Headwind and crosswind from a true wind and a runway
concepts.au_us: Shared trigonometry. Runway headings in the store are true, from OurAirports. A METAR wind is true. Do not apply magnetic variation unless the card is about the magnetic heading, and do not invent the variation.

concepts.title: Which TAF group first crosses a stated ceiling or visibility
concepts.au_us: The arithmetic of 'which group is worse' is shared. The legal alternate test is not. Australia uses the AIP alternate minima and the INTER/TEMPO planning rules. The US uses 14 CFR 91.169 and the part 121 minima. A live card states a teaching threshold in metres and feet. It does not claim to be the AIP or the CFR.

concepts.title: Wind correction angle and drift
concepts.au_us: Shared. Max drift is at the wind abeam. A live card needs a route the store does not yet have, so this stays a mechanism question.

concepts.title: Cruising level from magnetic track
concepts.au_us: Both use a hemispheric / semicircular rule on magnetic track, and the tables are not the same. Australia teaches the AIP table, including the VFR offset. The US teaches 14 CFR 91.179. Do not grade one table against the other. practiceLocale is required.

concepts.title: Point of safe return
concepts.au_us: Shared idea: the point from which the destination and the departure alternate are equal in fuel. The ATPL exam uses a specific chart method. Teach the equality. Do not copy a CASA exam plot.

concepts.title: Pressure altitude from QNH and elevation
concepts.au_us: Shared definition: the altitude in the ISA with the same pressure. Australian QNH is hPa. US altimeter settings are inHg. The 30 ft per hPa rule is a sea-level approximation, and the card must say so.

concepts.title: Density altitude
concepts.au_us: Shared. Hot, high and humid all raise density altitude. US exam stems often use a Colorado airport in °F and inHg. Australian stems use °C, hPa and inland elevation. Convert the inputs. Do not convert the physics.

concepts.title: What lengthens the takeoff roll
concepts.au_us: Shared factors: density altitude up, weight up, tailwind, slope up, contaminated surface. The CASA P-chart and the FAA performance chart are different artefacts. The mechanism is teachable. The chart-reading item is bank-only and must be an original chart, not a scanned exam plate.

concepts.title: Loading, moment and the centre of gravity
concepts.au_us: Shared moments. An aft centre of gravity reduces stall speed and stability. The worked loading needs an aircraft the store does not have.

concepts.title: Lift depends on density, speed and angle
concepts.au_us: Shared. Lift is one half rho V squared S CL. A gust changes V and can change angle of attack. Neither syllabus treats 'more power' as a term in the lift equation.

concepts.title: Induced drag and the back of the power curve
concepts.au_us: Shared. Induced drag rises as speed falls, so on the back side a higher nose without more power can increase the descent rate.

concepts.title: Stall is an angle of attack
concepts.au_us: Shared. Critical angle does not move because the airspeed indicator does. Stall speed indicated does move with weight, load factor and configuration.

concepts.title: Load factor in a level turn
concepts.au_us: Shared. A level 60° bank is 2 g, and stall speed rises with the square root of load factor. The critical angle is unchanged.

concepts.title: Manoeuvre speed and a gust
concepts.au_us: Shared. At or below Va the wing is meant to stall before the limit load is reached. Va falls as weight falls. A live gust on the map can be the stem. The key is the mechanism, not today's peak gust.

concepts.title: What a blocked pitot or static does to the instruments
concepts.au_us: Shared instrument errors. The altimeter and the ASI are pressure instruments. The failure case does not depend on whether the subscale is hPa or inHg.

concepts.title: Why airframe ice forms above the freezing level in cloud
concepts.au_us: Shared. Supercooled drops freeze on an airframe that is at or below 0 °C. The system details (boots, bleed air, weeping wing) are bank-only and aircraft-specific.

concepts.title: Cabin altitude and time of useful consciousness
concepts.au_us: Shared physiology. Certification cabin-altitude limits and the oxygen rules are different documents (CASR / Part 91 MOS against 14 CFR 91.211). The limit is bank-only. The partial-pressure reason is the physics card.

concepts.title: Hypoxic hypoxia and partial pressure
concepts.au_us: Shared. Oxygen stays about 21% by volume. Partial pressure falls as total pressure falls, so time of useful consciousness falls with altitude. Duty-time and FRMS rules are a different card and are bank-only.

concepts.title: Vestibular illusions in cloud
concepts.au_us: Shared. The leans, the somatogravic illusion and the coriolis illusion are the same mechanisms. The instrument-scan technique taught in the AFH and the IPH is the US wording of a recovery the Australian syllabus also requires.

concepts.title: Flight and duty limits
concepts.au_us: The physiology of fatigue is shared. The legal limits are not. CAO 48.1 and the CASRs are the Australian source. 14 CFR part 117 is the US flag source. practiceLocale is required. Do not blend the numbers.

concepts.title: When the altimeter goes to standard pressure
concepts.au_us: Australia transitions at 10,000 ft with the layer up to FL110. The United States transitions at 18,000 ft and FL180. A card that swaps these is testing the wrong country. The QNH on today's METAR can be the stem. The scored fact is the country's transition altitude.

concepts.title: When an alternate is required
concepts.au_us: Australia: AIP alternate minima, special alternate minima, and the planning treatment of INTER and TEMPO. United States: 14 CFR 91.169 for part 91, and the part 121 dispatch minima, which are not the 600-2 / 800-2 slogan unless the card cites the paragraph that still says so. Today's TAF can illustrate a group. The legal conclusion is bank-only and locale-specific.

concepts.title: Documents the licence stands on
concepts.au_us: Not interchangeable. Australian ATPL privileges are in CASR Part 61. US ATP privileges are in 14 CFR 61.167. A question written for one is not a translation of the other.

concepts.title: Low-level wind and gusts
concepts.au_us: The gust is the figure after G in both METAR traditions. Australian wind is knots true. The United States remote-pilot limit is a learning item under Part 107, not a shared number.

concepts.title: Cloud and visibility for a small unmanned aircraft
concepts.au_us: 14 CFR 107.51 states 3 statute miles and 500 ft below / 2,000 ft horizontal. CASA Part 101 standard RPA operating conditions require visual line of sight and remaining clear of cloud. The numbers are not a translation.

concepts.title: Density altitude, performance and battery
concepts.au_us: Hot, high and humid thin the air in both countries. A small aircraft spends more power to hover. Units differ: hPa and °C against inHg and °F.

concepts.title: Thunderstorm avoidance for a small aircraft near the ground
concepts.au_us: The gust front can arrive before the rain in both countries. This card teaches the order. It is not a clearance to fly.

concepts.title: Reading a METAR and a TAF for a drone lesson
concepts.au_us: Both countries publish METAR and TAF. INTER and CAVOK are Australian. The lesson is which document owns the present and which owns the hour ahead.

concepts.au_us: United States joint and service doctrine is public domain. Australian Defence material is not cited here unless its licence is clearly open.
